title: 3D Viewer
summary: Keyboard-first 3D scene viewer and editor: outliner, transform, material and light inspector, primitive add menu (A), undo history, the first attached .glb/.gltf loaded as nodes, a view PNG export and a turntable contact sheet. Pick it to block out, light or inspect a 3D scene, or to turn a glTF model into stills.

scene.description: Initial primitives, in outliner order. Each item is one of { shape: box|sphere|plane|cylinder|torus, size?: [..] (box [w,h,d] 1s, sphere [r], plane [w,d], cylinder [r,h], torus [R,tube]), color?, roughness? 0..1, metalness? 0..1 } or { light: ambient|directional|point, color?, intensity? >= 0, range? (point) }, plus name?, position?, rotation? (Euler degrees), scale? as [x, y, z].

background.description: Theme surface around the viewport: 'background' runs the canvas edge to edge; 'card' or 'muted' frames it as an inset stage. The 3D canvas itself always clears to --background.

camera.description: Starting orbit camera: { azimuth, elevation (degrees), distance, fov (degrees), target?: [x, y, z] }. Missing keys keep these defaults.

grid.description: Show the ground grid on open (G toggles it; a saved view wins).

axes.description: Show the world axes on open (X toggles it; a saved view wins).

turntableFrames.description: Starting frame count of the turntable sheet, 4 to 24 (one full turn from the current azimuth).

customScript.description: JS run last as (t3template, options) to bolt on controls, panels, buttons and presets. See boltOn.

controls.description: Starting values for bolt-on controls, { controlId: value }, applied when customScript adds them (a saved edit wins).

boltOn.summary: options.customScript runs once as new Function('t3template', 'options', code) after the scene has loaded (the first glTF asset too, if attached and not restored) and the panels exist. Drive the scene through t3template.instances: scene (t3kit.scene3d: get, set, add, update, remove, load, frame, exportBlob) and history (t3kit.history). Scene writes are silent and not undo steps: a control edit records its step after its onChange runs, and other writes become a step through setValues({ nodes }, label) or on the next inspector edit. Call t3template.refresh() after silent scene writes so the inspector, outliner and status update. onChange runs on user edits only, not on load: read the control value and apply it in the script (see example). Image stages (addImageStage, addShaderStage) run on every exported PNG, the view export and the turntable sheet, not on the live WebGL viewport. EDL calls do not apply. Errors log '[t3template] customScript error: ...' and show in a dismissible banner.
api: addControl({ id, label?, type: 'slider'|'toggle'|'select'|'color'|'text'|'button', min = 0, max = 1, step?, default?, options?: ['a', { value, label }], placeholder?, rows?, panel?: 'Title' | element from addPanel, onChange?(value, t3template), onClick?(t3template) }) -> { id, element, get(), set(value), setLabel(text) }. Values: slider number, toggle boolean, select the option value, color '#rrggbb', text string. No panel = 'Extras'. onChange runs on user edits only (not on load, undo or presets). Every control edit is one undo step, named after the control and value.

addPanel(title | { title, open = true, position = 'top' }) -> the panel body element (append your own nodes; the same title returns the same panel). 'top' = before the Scene panel (in view on load); 'bottom' = after History.

addToolbarButton(label, onClick(t3template), { shortcut?: 'shift+f' | 'mod+j', title? }) -> button (in the header and the Commands palette, Cmd+K). Shortcuts in reservedShortcuts are taken.   refresh() re-renders the inspector, outliner, camera readout and status after silent scene writes.

export() -> Promise<{ files: [{ name, type, size, width, height }] }>: the current view as PNG at canvas size (CSS size x DPR, the Export PNG button, Shift+E), after image stages, sent to t3.workspace.attach and downloaded. Throws on failure. The turntable sheet (Turntable panel, Shift+R) is a separate PNG and also runs the image stages.

addImageStage(id, (ctx, controls) => void, { at? }) / addShaderStage(id, glsl, uniforms?) / removeStage(id): edits the exported PNG canvas in place. ctx = { canvas, context (2D), width, height, scale, phase: 'export', kind: 'view' | 'turntable', frames?, cols?, rows?, copy(), random(seed?) }; scale = width / 1024, so multiply pixel sizes by it. On the turntable the stage runs once on the whole sheet. Stages run in the order added; there is no live preview.

getValues() -> { nodes, selected, camera, grid, axes, snap, controls }.   setValues({ nodes?, selected?, camera?, grid?, axes?, snap? }, label?) -> Promise<values>: strict (unknown keys throw). nodes replaces the scene (node ids come from the scene; the selected id must exist). camera, grid, axes and snap are view settings and not undo steps; nodes and selected are one undo step.
addPreset(name, { nodes?, selected? }) / applyPreset(name): a preset is a scene state, as undo steps hold it (camera is not stored).   on('change', cb(values)) -> off.

instances: { scene (t3kit.scene3d), history (t3kit.history) }. scene.get().nodes lists nodes with ids, parents and mesh, material or light; scene.update(id, { position|rotation|scale|material|light|name|visible }) merges, null clears a key.
